Exercise 15.7.47 — Setting Up Mass, Center of Mass, and IzI_zIz​ Integrals

Problem. Set up, but do not evaluate, integral expressions for (a) the mass, (b) the center of mass, and (c) the moment of inertia about the zzz-axis. The solid is enclosed by the cylinder y=x2y = x^2y=x2 and the planes z=0z = 0z=0 and y+z=1y + z = 1y+z=1; ρ(x,y,z)=x2+y2\rho(x,y,z) = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}ρ(x,y,z)=x2+y2​.

Describing the solid

Step 0.1: The region and its bounds.

The parabolic cylinder y=x2y=x^2y=x2 and the slanted plane y+z=1y+z=1y+z=1 meet where z=1−y=1−x2z = 1-y = 1-x^2z=1−y=1−x2. This curve reaches z=0z=0z=0 (the bottom plane) exactly at x=±1x = \pm 1x=±1, y=1y = 1y=1. Hence the solid projects onto the region −1≤x≤1-1 \le x \le 1−1≤x≤1, x2≤y≤1x^2 \le y \le 1x2≤y≤1 in the xyxyxy-plane, and at each such (x,y)(x,y)(x,y) the height runs from z=0z=0z=0 up to z=1−yz = 1-yz=1−y:

−1≤x≤1,x2≤y≤1,0≤z≤1−y. -1 \le x \le 1, \qquad x^2 \le y \le 1, \qquad 0 \le z \le 1 - y. −1≤x≤1,x2≤y≤1,0≤z≤1−y.

We use the order dz dy dxdz\,dy\,dxdzdydx in all three parts. The top point of the solid is (0,0,1)(0,0,1)(0,0,1); the bottom is the parabolic region x2≤y≤1x^2 \le y \le 1x2≤y≤1 in the plane z=0z=0z=0.

Part 1 — (a) The mass

Step 1.1: Set up the mass integral.

Insert ρ=x2+y2\rho = \sqrt{x^2+y^2}ρ=x2+y2​ and the bounds from Step 0.1:

Step 3.2: Verification of the setup by Python.

The script solution/part1_step1.py verifies the setup (the published answers above are the setups only, as the problem requires): (a) symbolically it confirms the wall meets the top plane at z=1−x2z = 1-x^2z=1−x2, which hits z=0z=0z=0 at x=±1x=\pm1x=±1; (b) point-membership tests confirm the bounds −1≤x≤1-1\le x\le 1−1≤x≤1, x2≤y≤1x^2\le y\le 1x2≤y≤1, 0≤z≤1−y0\le z\le 1-y0≤z≤1−y describe the enclosed solid; (c) a Monte-Carlo count gives a region volume 0.53320.53320.5332, matching the exact symbolic volume 8/158/158/15, and the Monte-Carlo averages of ρ\rhoρ, xρx\rhoxρ, yρy\rhoyρ, zρz\rhozρ, and (x2+y2)ρ(x^2+y^2)\rho(x2+y2)ρ over the region are all finite and consistent with the integrands above (the average of xρx\rhoxρ is about 000, as the symmetry note predicts). No integral is evaluated as an answer, per the problem statement. The figure script part1_figure1.py produces the sketch above.
